original_quote: One of the more surprising things I've noticed while working on Y Combinator is how frightening the most ambitious startup ideas are. Any one of them could make you a billionaire. 1. A new search engine. 2. Replace email. 3. Replace universities. 4. Internet drama. 5. The next Steve Jobs. 6. Bring back Moore's Law. 7. Ongoing diagnosis.
why_unfinished: PG published a flagship list of seven specific billion-dollar bets in 2012 but never returned to assess which panned out, died, or why — despite a decade of public evidence on each front.

original_quote: So I think VC funds are seriously threatened by the super-angels.
why_unfinished: PG declared super-angels an existential threat to traditional VC in 2010, but never returned to assess whether the threat materialized — even though top VCs ended the 2010s stronger than ever, a striking falsification he never publicly reckoned with.

original_quote: If you could get the right ten thousand people to move from Silicon Valley to Buffalo, Buffalo would become Silicon Valley. You only need two kinds of people to create a technology hub: rich people and nerds.
why_unfinished: PG asserted that transplanting 10,000 specific people could replicate Silicon Valley anywhere, but never explored why no one tried this or whether the thesis held as tech hubs actually emerged in Austin, Berlin, Miami, and others.
